transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
It's this cough — it just won't go away. It started about three weeks ago after I had a cold.
Thanks for sharing that. Could you tell me a bit more about how this cough is affecting your day-to-day life, and whether you have any allergies or bad reactions to any medicines?
It's mainly my sleep — the coughing fits wake me most nights, and I'd rate it about a 6 out of 10. As for medicines, I've never had any bad reactions, no known allergies.
Could you tell me about any medicines you take regularly or have started recently, and about any long-term health problems, past illnesses, operations, or hospital stays you've had?

I've got COPD, had it about 8 years now. For that I use a blue salbutamol inhaler — usually twice a day, but lately it's been 4 to 5 times a day — plus a Fostair 100/6 inhaler, two puffs twice daily. I also take lisinopril 10 mg once a day for my blood pressure, been on that several years.

I haven't had any operations or hospital stays. I did smoke 20 cigarettes a day for 40 years, but I stopped 10 years ago.
Can you tell me more about the cough — where you feel it, whether it stays in one place or moves, and anything else you've noticed along with it?

I can't say it's in one particular spot — it's just a chest cough, nothing that moves around. I'm bringing up white-to-yellow phlegm, more than my usual morning phlegm.

The other thing I've noticed is I get a bit more breathless than usual walking to the shop. No blood when I cough, no weight loss, no night sweats, and no chest pain.
What kinds of things have you noticed make your cough better or worse, like what you’re doing, how you’re sitting or lying, or anything you eat or take?
Cold air sets it off, and so does talking for a long time. Steam inhalation helps it a little. It tends to be worst in the morning and at night, and the coughing fits last a few minutes each.
Is there anything else you take for your health that we haven’t talked about yet?
No, that's everything — just the two inhalers and the lisinopril for my blood pressure. I don't take anything else.
What worries you most about this cough, and what are you hoping we can help with?

I suppose what worries me most is that my lungs are getting worse, or that it could be cancer. The cough's been going on three weeks now and I'm needing my blue inhaler far more than usual, so I'd like to get it checked out.

We've talked about your COPD and that you haven't had any operations or hospital stays — is there anything else from your past health, like other long-term conditions or illnesses, that you think I should know about?
No, nothing else I can think of — it's just the COPD and my blood pressure. That's all the long-term stuff I've got.
Apart from what you've already told me, have you noticed anything else that's come along with the cough?
No, I don't think there's anything else. Just the breathlessness when I walk to the shop, and the phlegm I mentioned.

Is there anything else you're taking that I should know about — any other regular medicines, anything new or changed recently, or anything you've bought over the counter, and if so, what and how much?
No, nothing new and nothing over the counter. The only change is that blue inhaler — I'm using it 4 to 5 times a day now instead of my usual twice.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
